scenes.headline: How a 35B agent scales horizon instead of size
scenes.sub: Agents-A1: verified long trajectories, specialist teachers, one small student.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Berry! Agents-A1 has about three billion active parameters, yet reaches the agent benchmarks of trillion-parameter models. Here's how.

scenes.text: Scale the horizon, not the parameters: train on verified long agent runs across six domains, then fold six specialists into one student.
scenes.mark: Scale the horizon, not the parameters
scenes.say: The idea: scale the horizon, not the parameters. Long, verified agent runs, then six specialists folded into one student.

steps.say: Each domain gets a knowledge-action graph: evidence, actions, observations, and verifiers.
A proposer samples part of the graph and poses a constrained task. A solver attacks it with retrieval and tools.
A verifier checks the answer, the evidence, the execution result, and whether the solver took a shortcut.
Each accepted step is logged: state, action, observation, verifier outcome. That record is what the model trains on.

items.say: First, fine-tune on about a hundred thousand trajectories across all domains.
Second, train a specialist teacher per domain, each going deep where a generalist would be pulled thin.
Third, the student generates its own rollouts, and each one is supervised only by its own domain's teacher.

steps.label: The teacher's full distribution
steps.say: At every position of the student's rollout, the teacher puts some probability on every token in the vocabulary.

steps.label: Only the teacher's top-k
steps.note: renormalised onto that support, then matched
steps.say: The loss keeps only the teacher's top few tokens, renormalises both distributions there, and matches them. The low-probability tail is dropped.

scenes.title: FrontierScience-Research
scenes.note: it doesn't win everywhere: GPT-5.5 leads web search and engineering
scenes.say: On FrontierScience-Research, the base model scores two point five. After training, forty, above GPT-5.5 and both trillion-parameter models. It doesn't win everywhere.

scenes.text: The recipe is the contribution: verified long-horizon data, and on-policy distillation that folds specialists into one small model.

recap: A knowledge-action graph makes verified agent data
Top-k alignment keeps what the teacher means
scenes.say: To recap: a graph that makes verified agent data, specialist teachers, and one student distilled on its own rollouts.
